The map's label for the lands of the Mon in Lower Burma, along the coast and the river deltas, shown in 800, 1100 and 1200. The Mon were among the earliest Theravada Buddhists in the region and called their land Ramanna.

Burmese chronicles tell of a Mon kingdom at Thaton and of the founding of Pegu. Most of these early dates come from chronicles written centuries later and are uncertain. The best known story says that Anawrahta of Pagan conquered Thaton in 1057 and carried its monks, scriptures and craftsmen north, and that Mon script and art then shaped Pagan (Theravada adopted at Pagan). Some historians doubt how much of this happened.

In the 1100 and 1200 snapshots Lower Burma was under Pagan. After Pagan fell, the Mon rose again in the kingdom of Hanthawaddy from 1287.
